thread:
alex-support: FYI customer ACME reported a sharp p99 latency regression starting ~2026-03-15 09:10 UTC. They see long tails and occasional 5-10s responses.

julia-sre: Do we have traces? any OOMs or GRPC errors?

alex-support: Customer attached a short capture. No OOM crash, but worker-side GC spikes and repeated slab compactions in logs. Heap usage climbs and KV cache evictions spike before p99 climbs.

lee-runtime: Can you paste the trimmed runtime logs and allocator stats? also which model + quantization?

alex-support: Model: gpt-small-v1 q4_0, tenant uses multi-tenant host routing. Logs excerpt:

```
2026-03-15T09:09:58Z worker[pid=342]: kv_cache.size=1.9GB kv_evictions=420
2026-03-15T09:10:01Z worker[pid=342]: slab.compact.start free_frag=12%
2026-03-15T09:10:03Z worker[pid=342]: p99.latency=3.8s p95=1.1s
2026-03-15T09:10:10Z worker[pid=342]: slab.compact.end free_frag=8% alloc_retry=12
```

mike-eng: That pattern smells like fragmentation + KV growth. Multi-tenant tenant had a sudden burst of long contexts? Any trace of unusually large prefix caches?

alex-support: Customer says they sent a few hundred long (>2048) chat chains during the window.

julia-sre: Steps to repro and short-term mitigations: 1) reproduce on staging with same tenant traffic pattern 2) enable active fallback routing to a smaller KV-preserving model variant 3) force GC/compaction schedule tweak 4) safe rolling restart to free fragmented GPU slabs.

lee-runtime: For repro, try a short script that does many variable-length requests to simulate heap/KV churn. Example curl loop for reproducer:

```
for i in {1..500}; do
  len=$(( (RANDOM % 3000) + 200 ))
  python3 -c "print('x'*$len)" | curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d @- &
  sleep 0.02
done
```

mike-eng: Also capture allocator stats endpoint `/internal/allocator/stats` every 10s during the run. Look for grow_rate, num_splits, slab_unused_pct.

oncall-bot: scheduled snapshot: allocator-stats @ 2134567920 (auto)

alex-support: Customer agreed to a short canary: route 10% of traffic to a variant with persistent KV eviction policy set to LRU and a slightly smaller max_prefix_kv.

julia-sre: Long-term fixes: - KV cap heuristics that auto-shrink per-tenant on high fragmentation - allocator tune: reduce slab size and increase compaction aggressiveness at >75% slab age - migrate heavy long-context tenants to dedicated capacity.

lee-runtime: Quick toggle we can run now (safe, non-disruptive): set `runtime.flags.kv_evict_threshold_percent=65` for the pool serving this tenant and enable `allocator.flags.compaction_hint=aggressive` for 10m window. That should reduce tail while we validate.

mike-eng: Will explain impacts to customer: might increase token CPU but reduce p99. Also we'll watch for degraded throughput.

alex-support: I applied the kv_evict_threshold change on the staging pool and saw p99 drop from ~4.2s to ~600ms under repro load. Pushing to prod canary now for 10% traffic.

julia-sre: Please attach the heatmap and flamegraph links once available. Also mark this thread with incident tag if p99 doesn't improve in 30m.

alex-support: Heatmap: https://telemetry.redwood/heatmaps/2134567890-kv-growth.png
Flamegraph: https://telemetry.redwood/flame/2134567890-alloc-flame.html

lee-runtime: Good signal. Next steps if still high: schedule rolling node restarts to defragment GPU memory and consider per-tenant KV hard cap fallback with reject-oversize flag.

mike-eng: I'll draft a short postmortem checklist for the customer: observed metrics, repro commands, mitigation toggles, and recommended capacity path (dedicated).

alex-support: Customer accepted canary and saw immediate improvement. They'll keep us posted if they resume long-context bursts. Closing loop after 24h monitoring. :white_check_mark:
